Not every error justifies a retry.
HTTP 400 (fout in je verzoek — een retry: HTTP 400 (error in your request — a retry produces the same result)
HTTP 401/403 (authenticatie- of autorisa: HTTP 401/403 (authentication or authorization error — refresh the token first)
Validatiefouten vanuit Twinfield (fout i: Validation errors from Twinfield (error in the booking data)
wacht na een mislukte poging steeds iets: wait slightly longer after a failed attempt before the next attempt. Set a maximum number of attempts (for example 3 to 5) and a maximum wait time. Add a small random delay (jitter) to spread simultaneous retries from multiple processes.
Bij financiële integraties is idempotent: In financial integrations, idempotency is crucial. A booking created twice leads to errors in your administration.
stuur bij iedere boeking een unieke exte: send a unique external reference with every booking (for example your own order-ID or document number). Twinfield lets you find previously created transactions this way.
houd in je eigen systeem bij welke aanro: keep track in your own system of which calls have been completed successfully. Check before a retry whether the operation may have already succeeded on the Twinfield side.
bij twijfel: bevraag Twinfield eerst of: if in doubt: query Twinfield first to see whether the document already exists before you create it again.
Bouw dit in vóórdat je in productie gaat: Build this in before you go into production. Fixing duplicate bookings is laborious and error-prone.
Twinfield retourneert fouten als SOAP-fa: Twinfield returns errors as SOAP faults or as error codes in the XML response. Always process these explicitly:
op applicatieniveau en log de faultcode: at application level and log the faultcode and faultstring
— verwerk een boeking alleen volledig of: — process a booking only completely or not at all
bij herhaalde fouten op dezelfde operati: when repeated errors occur on the same operation; this points to a structural problem
Vermijd stille fouten waarbij een aanroe: Avoid silent failures where a call fails but your system continues as if everything is fine. This leads to inconsistencies between your own system and Twinfield that are difficult to trace.

Stap 2 — Test authenticatie en tokenverl: Step 2 — Test authentication and token expiration - Verify the complete OAuth flow end-to-end - Simulate an expired access token and verify that your refresh logic works correctly - Test what happens with an invalid refresh token
Stap 3 — Test foutscenario's expliciet -: Step 3 — Test error scenarios explicitly - Send an invalid CompanyCode — what happens? - Send a malformed SOAP message — is the error caught correctly? - Simulate a timeout — does the retry logic trigger correctly? - Send the same booking twice — does your idempotency logic prevent duplication?
Stap 4 — Valideer logging - Controleer d: Step 4 — Validate logging - Check that logs do not contain tokens - Verify that correlation IDs are passed through correctly - Check that error logs contain sufficient detail for debugging
Stap 5 — Voer een acceptatietest uit met: Step 5 — Perform acceptance testing with an accountant or financial manager Have someone with accounting knowledge verify the resulting transactions in Twinfield before going live. Technical success does not automatically mean bookkeeping-correct data.
